comparability.reason: The study provides quantitative data on PFAS concentration and concentration factor in an ion exchange still-bottom concentrate and describes a plasma-plus-RO closed-loop management scheme, but lacks sufficient detail on membrane operating conditions, performance metrics, energy use, and destruction efficiency to allow quantitative comparison with other membrane residuals management studies.

endpoints.interpretation: Study focuses on destruction of PFAS in a distilled ion-exchange still-bottom concentrate using plasma vortex technology; treated still bottom is further polished by reverse osmosis, and RO retentate is returned to the plasma system, forming a closed loop with no liquid discharge. Extent of destruction is not quantified in the provided text.
endpoints.reported_term: PFAS Destruction in IX Still Bottoms with Plasma Vortex Technology

endpoints.interpretation: Reverse osmosis polishing of the treated still bottom, combined with recycling of RO retentate back to the plasma treatment unit, results in a treatment loop where there is no net liquid discharge from the concentrate management system.
endpoints.reported_term: closed loop with no liquid discharge

limitations.statement: Concentrate originates from ion exchange media regeneration rather than directly from a membrane separation step; membrane involvement is limited to a reverse osmosis polishing step applied after plasma treatment.
Energy consumption and cost for the plasma vortex destruction and reverse osmosis polishing steps are not reported in the provided material.

matrix.value: Distilled PFAS concentrate (ion exchange still bottom) subjected to plasma destruction and subsequent reverse osmosis polishing

pfas_scope.value: Total PFAS (approximately 640 mg/L in still bottom concentrate)

quantitative_findings.name: PFAS concentration in distilled still-bottom concentrate
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: reported as approximately 640 mg/L total PFAS in 45 L of distilled PFAS concentrate (still bottom) recovered after IX media regeneration

quantitative_findings.name: Volume of distilled PFAS still-bottom concentrate recovered
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: forty-five liters of a distilled PFAS concentrate (still bottom) recovered after ion exchange media regeneration

quantitative_findings.name: Overall PFAS concentration factor from original water to still bottom
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: reported as an overall concentration factor of about thirty thousand relative to the original PFAS-containing water

residuals_byproducts.statement: Reverse osmosis retentate from polishing of the treated still bottom is returned to the plasma treatment system, forming a closed loop with no liquid discharge; residual liquid concentrates are thus internally recycled rather than discharged.

treatment.value: Plasma vortex destruction of PFAS in ion exchange still bottoms, followed by reverse osmosis polishing with RO retentate recycled to plasma system (closed-loop, no liquid discharge)

records.citation: Authors not fully visible. PFAS Destruction Using Supercritical Water Oxidation (SCWO) at Peterson Space Force Base. Journal of Environmental Engineering. 2025.

comparability.reason: The record documents a field-scale RO+SCWO treatment train for PFAS-impacted water and highlights that RO concentration can lower SCWO energy and reactor volume requirements, but it does not report quantitative performance, recovery, concentration factors, or energy metrics. These data are therefore mainly useful to describe treatment-train configuration and conceptual management of membrane-derived PFAS concentrates rather than to support quantitative comparison with other technologies.

endpoints.interpretation: Reverse osmosis was used to separate and concentrate PFAS from PFAS-impacted aqueous streams into a smaller-volume concentrate stream prior to SCWO; this is a phase-separation/concentration step rather than destruction.

Supercritical water oxidation was applied to the RO-concentrated PFAS stream with the stated purpose of PFAS destruction; accessible text emphasizes destruction intent and efficiency/energy considerations but does not report explicit numerical destruction efficiencies or defluorination metrics.
endpoints.reported_term: PFAS destruction using supercritical water oxidation

limitations.statement: Evidence available is limited to high-level description of the treatment train (RO concentration followed by SCWO) with no reported numerical values for RO recovery, concentration factor, PFAS concentrations, SCWO destruction efficiency, energy use, or costs.

The deployment is described only for PFAS-impacted aqueous streams at a single site (Peterson Space Force Base), so applicability to other water types or membrane concentrate compositions is not characterized in the accessible text.

matrix.value: PFAS-impacted aqueous streams (site waters) at Peterson Space Force Base; specific composition and PFAS species not detailed in accessible text.

operating_conditions.name: treatment_train_configuration
operating_conditions.value: RO used as a concentration step prior to SCWO to increase PFAS concentration in a smaller volume stream and improve SCWO efficiency.

operating_conditions.name: process_rationale
operating_conditions.value: Concentrating PFAS by RO prior to SCWO reduces overall SCWO energy use and reactor volume requirements.

pfas_scope.value: PFAS (unspecified mixtures in PFAS-impacted aqueous streams; individual compounds and concentrations not reported in accessible text).

residuals_byproducts.statement: RO generates a PFAS-enriched concentrate stream that is subsequently treated by SCWO; the study positions this as a way to manage membrane-derived PFAS concentrates by routing them to thermal-oxidative destruction under supercritical water conditions.

study_scale.value: Field deployment at Peterson Space Force Base using reverse osmosis (RO) followed by supercritical water oxidation (SCWO) for PFAS-impacted aqueous streams.

treatment.value: Two-stage treatment train: reverse osmosis (RO) used to concentrate PFAS upstream, followed by supercritical water oxidation (SCWO) for PFAS destruction.
